text:
sasha: Heads-up — our spot savings streak for west-us2 mixed pools collapsed yesterday. running a quick FinOps sketch, and I think we need to tweak the safety margin and the chargeback cadence.

matt: saw that. eviction spike ~01:30 UTC, ~18% of jobs got restarted. k8s-bot has logs.

k8s-bot: eviction-events: 2024-11-03T01:28:34Z -> preemption signal on node gpu-mix-3f. affected pods: 42, avg restart time 120s.

sasha: rough numbers from the sample window: spot avg price discount vs on-demand: 62%, but realized savings (after restarts + latency penalty) dropped to ~40%. variance spiked too (stddev 14% -> 26%).

leah: can you drop the quick calc for realized savings? finance needs a reproducible formula.

sasha: yep. simple form I used: \n\n```\nrealized_savings = (on_demand_cost - (spot_cost + restart_cost + latency_cost)) / on_demand_cost\nrestart_cost = restart_time_seconds / 3600 * on_demand_hourly_rate * tasks_affected_factor\nlatency_cost = (SLO_penalty_tokens * token_cost) + engineering_overtime_estimate\n```\n
sasha: numbers: on_demand_hourly ~ $3.20, spot_hourly average paid $1.22, restart_cost (estimated) $0.18/hr equivalent across pool, latency_cost ~ $0.05/hr eq. gives realized: (3.2 - (1.22+0.18+0.05))/3.2 ≈ 39%

matt: that matches my quick internal: we tend to undercount the tail restarts because short jobs regenerate quickly but long chat sessions pay the latency.

oliver: question — are we charging teams based on nominal spot price or realized cost? current chargeback uses nominal spot paid rate + a small interruption reserve.

finance-bot: charging_policy: spot_paid_rate + fixed_preemptible_buffer (0.05 USD/hr) for now. historical reconciliation monthly.

leah: ok that buffer isn't holding up. propose: move to an "effective-price" metric for chargeback computed weekly: effective_price = (total_cloud_spend_on_pool + ops_recovery_costs) / total_effective_gpu_hours. Then bill teams that week at effective_price for their hours. This smooths variance and keeps teams accountable.

sasha: +1 from infra POV. But we should add a safety-floor: never bill above on_demand_price and never below 35% of on_demand for spot-heavy pools (to keep incentives).

oliver: ops asks: how do we handle sudden regional preemption storms? proposal: keep 10% of pool in on-demand reserved capacity as an automatic backstop, and use color-coded routing to shift critical traffic.

matt: 10% feels high for steady-state. we could make it adaptive: reserve_pct = min( max( observed_eviction_rate * 1.5, 2%), 12%) — tuned weekly.

leah: can we simulate budget effects? I created a tiny model in the sheet: https://drive.internal/r/redwood/finops/spot-model (internal) — inputs: eviction_rate, average_spot_discount, restart_penalty_seconds, on_demand_hourly.

sasha: ran a run: with 8% eviction and avg discount 60% we get weekly effective_price ≈ $1.98/hr (vs nominal spot $1.12). 

oliver: that delta is pretty material to teams. If we switch to effective_price billing weekly they might complain. we should phase it and show pro-forma comparisons.

leah: agree. rollout plan: 
- week 0: run simulation and share team-level impact reports
- week 1-2: opt-in effective_price for a subset of teams (platform + search)
- week 3: default to effective_price for new projects; existing can opt-in
- month 2: full default with opt-out window and 1 month notice

matt: ops action: reduce eviction tail by tuning preemption buffer on the node bootstrap: add `--preemptible-safety-margin=7` to mixed nodegroup launcher and increase spot requeue backoff for long jobs. testing on staging.

sasha: one more thing — we need to expose the realized_savings and effective_price per-team in Console so eng teams can understand their monthly delta. Product/console roadmap ticket needed.

oliver: I'll open a console ticket and link the model.

leah: finance wants a simple chargeback field added to the weekly SKU export: `effective_gpu_price_usd` and `eviction_rate_pct`.

finance-bot: created ticket FIN-5423 for adding fields to weekly export.

matt: quick blockers: we need metrics for restart_cost per-job class (short/medium/long). Sasha can you capture a sample by EOD?

sasha: yes — I'll grab 72h sample and dump to the sheet.

oliver: I'll prototype adaptive reserve and run it in west-us2 for 48h canary.

leah: I'll prepare comms and a pro-forma two-week impact mail to platform teams.

sasha: summary: (1) implement weekly effective_price chargeback model in spreadsheet, (2) infra to run reserve canary + node bootstrap safety_margin tweak, (3) Console ticket for visibility, (4) finance export changes, (5) comms + phased rollout. owners: infra(matt/sasha/oliver), finance(leah), product(oliver).

matt: noted. assigning infra tasks in JIRA after canary. :thumbsup:

oliver: thanks — will post canary results and the evictions dashboard link here once live.

sasha: thanks all.

leah: :+1:

k8s-bot: canary started (west-us2) at 2024-11-04T03:00:00Z, reserved_pct=6%

sasha: last note — if effective_price spikes above 10% of on_demand in any week, automatic rollback to nominal billing and an incident review.

leah: agreed.

matt: copy, monitoring alerts added.

oliver: will follow up with data in ~72h.
